outcome: Declare blockers and combat damage steps are skipped when no creature attacks, and a second combat damage step occurs when an attacker or blocker has first strike or double strike.

note: defines attacking and defending player roles

outcome: Only creatures are offered as legal attackers or blockers, and only players, planeswalkers and battles as attack targets.
A noncreature permanent put onto the battlefield attacking or blocking enters but is not an attacking or blocking permanent.
A creature put onto the battlefield attacking under a non-attacking player's control enters but is not attacking.
A creature put onto the battlefield attacking a player not in the game or an invalid permanent enters but is not attacking.
A creature put onto the battlefield attacking after blockers are declared enters unblocked.
A creature put onto the battlefield blocking an attacker not attacking its controller or their planeswalker or battle enters but is not blocking.
A creature that is also a battle put onto the battlefield attacking or blocking enters but is not attacking or blocking.
A resolving effect that would make a battle an attacking or blocking creature does nothing for that part.

A permanent leaving the battlefield, changing controller, phasing out, regenerating, or ceasing to be a creature, planeswalker or battle is removed from combat and stops attacking, blocking, blocked or unblocked.
A creature already declared as an attacker or blocker stays in combat when an effect would have kept it from attacking or blocking.
Tapping or untapping a declared attacker or blocker leaves it in combat and it still deals combat damage.
An attacker whose planeswalker or battle target left combat stays attacking, may be blocked, and deals no combat damage if unblocked.
A blocking planeswalker creature is removed from combat only if it stops being both a creature and a planeswalker.
An attacked planeswalker battle is removed from combat only when it stops being both, or stops being a battle while not controlled by its protector.

note: defines 'had to attack' for abilities that check it; those abilities' rules cover the outcome
introduces timing restrictions relative to combat points

outcome: A spell restricted to before or after attackers are declared is castable only before or after the declare attackers step begins, whether or not attackers exist.
A spell restricted to before or after blockers are declared is castable only before or after the declare blockers step begins, whether or not blockers exist.
A spell restricted to 'during combat' is castable at an appropriate time in any combat phase of the turn.
A spell with a before/after combat-point restriction but no 'during combat' wording is castable only relative to the first combat phase of the turn.
A 'only before' restriction on a skipped step is castable only before the declare attackers step ends, or before the precombat main phase ends if combat is skipped.
A spell castable only during combat after blockers are declared is not castable when the declare blockers step is skipped.
The combat timing restrictions apply equally to activated abilities.
